_comment: Object keys and whether the server stores an object under them (backend/internal/storage/storagepath, ValidateKey). A key is at most max_key_bytes bytes of UTF-8 without control characters (Unicode category Cc), in segments of at most max_segment_bytes bytes separated by '/', none of them empty, '.' or '..': no leading or trailing '/', no '//'. max_key_bytes is S3's 1024-byte path less the tenant id, the longest collection segment and two separators, so the key fits in every collection; max_segment_bytes is the longest file name a filer-backed store (SeaweedFS) takes. The server, both SDKs' fakes and the console refuse every key under refused as INVALID_ARGUMENT where an object is created; an empty key is not listed, as a caller that names none gets one from the server. Each lengths case is a key of segments joined by '/', each segment unit repeated to the bytes given, counted in UTF-8. Invalid UTF-8 has no place in JSON, so each consumer tests it in its own language.
